sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
sources.independent_condition_review: BagIt 1.0 treats payload as opaque bytes. Complete/valid are package-relative, not an expected interview inventory. Creation and validation tools must support SHA-256 and SHA-512; SHA-512 is recommended for new bags, not a guaranteed observed default. All tag-manifest checksums count as well. No active-attack guarantee.
sources.independent_semantic_assessment: The final conditions historical continuity on an attributable earlier reference and scope; present hashes cannot witness an earlier undocumented move. This temporal conclusion is reviewer reasoning, consistent with the specified mechanism.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0
sources.independent_condition_review: Intellectual Entity, Representation, File and Bitstream are Object categories in v3. Event identifier, type and date/time are mandatory. Detail and outcome containers are optional; supplied containers have their own child constraints. Specific time and zone are recommendations. Repositories may record some actions in other logs.
sources.independent_semantic_assessment: Supports typed relation/event proposals and prohibits interpreting missing optional details as proof no migration occurred. The proposed ledger deliberately records more than the minimum standard; that is a design choice, not a claim of mandatory PREMIS fields.

sources.title: Archivematica issue #346: md5deep checksum validation for multiple files with same checksum
sources.independent_condition_review: The AM 1.7.2/Ubuntu 16.04 report describes aggregate error 110 despite per-file passes for duplicate digests. Closed status and 1.10.0 milestone do not alone establish a shipped fix.
sources.independent_semantic_assessment: Final reports a bounded historic case and calls for raw per-item results and independent checks. It does not declare a current regression. sources.independent_locator: Official DSpace 10.x package page, restore-mode subsections; captured in R17-web-search.json
sources.independent_condition_review: For AIP restore: -r collision backs out changes; -r -k skips an existing object and its children; existing collection/community prevents automatic restoration of its missing children. -r -f replaces contents with potential loss and attempts rollback on an error. Bulk traversal and supported modes depend on flags/plugin.
sources.independent_semantic_assessment: Final correctly compares default rollback, skip and replacement and warns of scope/access limits. It omits the parent/children special case, but offers no DSpace operational recommendation or assertion all missing items are recovered. Direct retrieval here also returned 403; official indexed text is the evidence, not a claimed successful direct open.
